origin.description: Multi-dimensional objects are written as a sequence of extents. A vector with no dimensions is written as its length.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The object whose dimensions are formatted.

origin.details: Extents are separated by a space, the times sign, and a space. With cli.unicode TRUE that sign is ×. A missing extent is ??. Thousands are grouped by formatC with format "d". The mark is a comma unless OutDec is a comma, in which case the mark is a dot. NULL has no dimensions and is written as 0.

translation.description: The same extents. A list with no dim uses its length. NULL is the pillar NULL sentinel and is written as 0.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, Matrix, DataFrame, Table, or NULL. A missing extent is None and is written as ??.

translation.details: The separator is a space, symbol["times"], and a space. cli.unicode TRUE uses × and FALSE uses x. OutDec comes from pillar._options.get_option("OutDec") and defaults to ".". The thousands mark is "," unless OutDec is ",", when the mark is ".".
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import Table
from pillar.summary import dim_desc

print(dim_desc(list(range(1, 11))))
print(dim_desc(Table((4, 2, 2, 2))))
